Figure 17c shows the out-of-plane electrical conductivities of Aluzine-based FS-TCCs prepared with varying microsphere concentrations (i.e., 0.1%, 1%, and 5% Ag-PMMA area coverage). An onset of electrical conductivity occurs at lamination pressures corresponding to the upper range of bond-line thicknesses (approx. 51µm). By slightly increasing the lamination pressure according to the microsphere concentration (Figure 16c), the electrical resistivities can be reduced to nearly undetectable levels (system resistance approx. 0.05 W·cm2) without a significant reduction in the polymer thickness. The power trendline approximating the relationship between out-of-plane conductivity and the lamination pressure illustrates excellent electrical conductivities, which approach the system resistance after sufficient reduction in polymer thickness. As shown in Figure 17d, optical transparencies are observed to scale with geometrical shading (i.e., microsphere concentration). FS-TCCs with 0.1% microsphere concentration demonstrate an averaged 28/52 DE-EE0010241 Nicolas Gaillard transparency greater than 90% in the 370nm-1200nm wavelength region, with a near proportional reduction with increased microsphere area coverage. (c) Out-of-plane electrical conductivities of FS-TCC samples (0.1%, 1%, and 5% Ag-PMMA by area) prepared under a range of lamination pressures. (d) Optical transparencies (averaged over the 370nm-1200nm wavelength region) of FS-TCC samples (0.1%, 1%, 5%, 10%, and 20% Ag-PMMA by area) compared to the estimated geometrical shading. Three samples were prepared for each concentration and measured for their optical transparencies. Aging and Characterization of Free-Standing TCCs: To evaluate the effect of aging on TCCs’ optical transparencies and out-of-plane conductivities, FS-TCCs were measured in their as-synthesized state and after outdoor aging. Special holders were designed to allow easy mounting and transport between systems, such as the electrical conductivity testbed (Figure 18a and b), the outdoor durability platform (Figure 18c), and the UV-visible spectroscopy instrument (Figure 18d: PerkinElmer Lambda 750S) to assist with sample handling and ensuring characterization was always performed on the same location of each sample (i.e., center area). Samples remained in the sample holder during characterization unless otherwise noted. The outdoor durability platform was located on the rooftop of the Hawaii Institute of Geophysics building at the University of Hawaii in Manoa (Honolulu, HI, USA, latitude 21.29831, longitude -157.81652, semi-arid tropical climate), and faced south with a 21° tilt (i.e., Honolulu’s latitude). The outdoor diurnal conditions were monitored using data provided by Western Weather Group’s University of Hawaii at Manoa Atmospheric Sciences Weather Data, measured using instruments located within a quarter mile of our outdoor test bed. During the 1,000-hour exposure period, samples were either intermittently removed from their testbed for characterization or remained untouched until the end to minimize potential artifacts that may arise from repeated measurements. Overall, FS-TCCs experienced daily average solar insolation, temperature, R.H., and precipitation of 6.56 kWh/m2, 26.12 °C, 71.54%, and 0.95 mm, respectively.
